response.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS cnt FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), sh AS (SELECT gender, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM per), av AS (SELECT gender, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM sh) SELECT gender, cnt AS order_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM av WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: A NULL gender, if any customer has one, counts as its own group and is included in the total and in the average of shares. The request does not say how to treat NULL genders.
The average share is the plain average of the per-gender shares, taken over the genders that appear after the inner joins.

alternatives.interpretation: Customers with a NULL gender are excluded, so they are not a gender group and do not count toward the total or the average.
alternatives.sql: WITH per AS (SELECT c.gender AS gender, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS cnt FROM Invoices i JOIN Orders o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.gender), sh AS (SELECT gender, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM per), av AS (SELECT gender, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM sh) SELECT gender, cnt AS order_count, share, share - avg_share AS share_minus_avg FROM av WHERE share > avg_share
